subtype: Approach: hypothesis testing with one change at a time [Thinking]
passage: Thursday, 1 am, finally quiet. The site went slow tonight, so I wrote my guess on a sticky note first: the pool of database connections has run dry. If that's true, raising the pool size a little should ease things. Changed only that. Waited ten minutes and watched the graph: waiting requests dropped, but errors stayed. So the guess was partly right, not the whole story. I didn't touch the timeout or the cache at the same time, even though Keerthana pinged, 'just try everything?' Next idea: a slow query hogging connections. One change again, a limit on that query, and the errors stopped. Notes are in the incident doc so the morning shift can see the order I tried things. Tired, pleased. — Kalyani

qa.a: Kalyani could ask a second engineer to compare the graphs from before and after, since fresh eyes may spot a pattern the first guess missed.

qa.a: Keerthana may find it slower than trying everything, but would likely value it later, since the notes show which change helped.
